summary: The package shows good CGM coverage and a complete active AAPS profile, with meaningful hypoglycemia risk and a recurring late-morning to afternoon rise. Automation is active and internally coherent, but meal attribution is weak because there are no carb treatment entries and no user-declared meal strategy fields to validate against. Overall, the safest synthesis is to keep current settings and verify patterns one at a time before any dependent change.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM quality is good with 3995 glucose entries over 14 days, 98.7% coverage, no invalid or duplicate entries, and an estimated 5-minute cadence. The active selected AAPS profile is complete for basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets, and SMB settings.
analysis_steps.evidence: Coverage_percent 98.7, gap_count 10, largest_gap_minutes 65.0, valid_entry_count 3995, invalid_entry_count 0, aaps_profile present and authoritative.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal timestamps or carb treatment entries; limited ability to isolate fasting-only periods from meal and correction effects.

analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia risk is clinically relevant: time below range is 5.1% overall, with several CGM readings in the low 40s mg/dL. Hyperglycemia is present but less dominant than the low risk. Variability remains moderate with CV 32.6%.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall time_below_range_percent 5.1, CV 32.6, glucose_extremes down to 41-42 mg/dL and up to 293 mg/dL, daily low-heavy days on Aug 11-14 and Aug 18.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No symptom logs or explicit severe-event confirmations; some lows and highs overlap with corrections, temp targets, and automation responses.

analysis_steps.findings: Local-time glucose suggests a recurring late-morning through afternoon rise and a recurring overnight/early-morning low tendency. The stepped basal profile may contribute, but the same windows also contain corrections, temp targets, and IOB effects, so basal causality is not separated cleanly.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local averages rise from about 110-162 mg/dL between 07:00-16:00 local, while 00:00-04:00 local averages are roughly 91-106 mg/dL. Daily lows appear on Aug 13-14 and Aug 21, and highs cluster around Aug 10, 14, 15, and 18.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting-only windows, no meal markers, and no activity log to separate basal from meal or exercise effects.

analysis_steps.findings: CR varies by time, ISF is fixed at 56 mg/dL/U, and DIA is 10 hours. Correction responses are highly variable across the period, which is consistent with the influence of meal timing, IOB, automation, and temp targets rather than a single profile parameter alone.
analysis_steps.evidence: CR segments are 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, and 12.6 g/U; ISF is 56 mg/dL/U; DIA is 10 h. Therapy response windows show delayed lows and rebounds after some corrections and steadier responses after others.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal bolus timestamps tied to meals, no carb entries, and no confirmed fasting correction-free tests to judge CR or ISF independently.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and configured coherently. SMB is allowed without COB and with temp targets, but not after carbs or with high temp targets. The automation stack is functioning as a response layer rather than the root cause of the observed glycemic pattern.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled true, uam_enabled true, smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_cob_enabled false, smb_after_carbs_enabled false, smb_with_temp_target_enabled true, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false. Representative loop statuses show SMB/UAM responses even when COB is 0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal logs to tell whether SMB/UAM is reacting to meals or to non-meal drift; algorithm-vs-user intent is not separable.

analysis_steps.findings: Classic Autosens is off by design, while dynamic sensitivity is active and the observed sensitivity_ratio of 1 is neutral rather than disabled. Observed enacted rates and IOB remain below max basal and max IOB limits, so no hard ceiling appears to be driving the pattern.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent 70, max_basal_u_per_hour 12, max_iob_units 25. Representative loop statuses show rates up to about 4 U/h and IOB up to about 5.9 U, both below caps.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No direct trace of why dynamic sensitivity changed on each loop; no fasting-only interval to prove whether automation is compensating for basal mismatch.

analysis_steps.findings: There is no user-declared meal strategy to compare against because analysis_context.meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Observed therapy windows are dominated by correction boluses and temp basal responses rather than documented meal boluses, so a general prebolus rule cannot be supported from this dataset.
analysis_steps.evidence: meal_strategies empty, strategy_stable_for_period null, carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0, insulin_entries 655, and therapy_response_windows show several correction windows with delayed lows or rebounds over 6 hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal timestamps, no bolus-to-meal timing, and no carb composition data; prebolus behavior cannot be validated per meal.

analysis_steps.findings: There is no evidence supporting e-carbs in the package. No carb treatment entries or extended carb entries are present, and the delayed variability seen in some windows is better explained by corrections and IOB than by a documented slow-carb pattern.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min null, and 6-hour response windows show mixed correction behavior rather than a clearly identified e-carb pattern.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked e-carb use, no carb duration entries, and no meal composition data to distinguish slow absorption from insulin stacking.

analysis_steps.findings: The safest synthesis is to keep current profile and AAPS settings unchanged for now. The main reason is unresolved causality: hypoglycemia risk is real, afternoon hyperglycemia is real, and both are still confounded by corrections, temp targets, SMB/UAM, dynamic sensitivity, and missing meal data. The package does not support changing dependent settings together.
analysis_steps.evidence: Good telemetry coverage, complete authoritative profile, lows into the 40s mg/dL, afternoon rise in local hourly glucose, active but coherent SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity, and no carb entries or declared meal strategy to validate meal-based tuning.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting-only proof window and no meal timing log to separate basal, CR, bolus timing, SMB/UAM, and correction effects.

strengths: CGM data quality is strong with 98.7% coverage and no invalid or duplicate entries.
The active AAPS profile is complete and internally coherent across basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets, and SMB settings.
The overnight period is often near target, suggesting not all hours are broadly overcorrected.
Automation limits were not exceeded in the observed windows; max basal and max IOB were not visibly binding.
issues: Overall hypoglycemia burden is meaningful, with time below range at 5.1% and multiple readings in the low 40s mg/dL.
A recurring late-morning to afternoon rise is visible in local-time glucose, with average values peaking around 14:00-16:00 local.
Correction and IOB responses are variable, with some windows showing delayed lows and rebounds that make basal versus meal attribution unclear.

recommendations.title: Hold basal profile and verify with a fasting-only window
recommendations.description: Overnight lows and late-morning/afternoon highs coexist, but corrections, temp targets, and missing meal data prevent a clean basal attribution. Keep the basal profile unchanged for now and verify with one fasting overnight or meal-free window before any basal edit.

suggested_change.verify: One overnight fasting segment with minimal corrections and no temporary target.

recommendations.title: Keep SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity unchanged
recommendations.description: The automation layer is coherent and within observed limits, and there is no evidence that max basal or max IOB ceilings are the main problem. Because lows are already present, changing SMB or sensitivity settings before basal and meal separation would raise risk.

suggested_change.verify: Watch for IOB buildup during low-risk periods without changing the automation settings.

recommendations.title: Defer prebolus and e-carb changes until meal timing is logged
recommendations.description: No carb entries, no declared meal strategy, and no documented e-carb use are available to support routine meal strategy changes. Keep current immediate bolus behavior unchanged and gather meal timing data before considering any prebolus or e-carb adjustment.

suggested_change.verify: Log meal timestamp, bolus timing, and any rescue carb use for one week.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current basal profile unchanged and verify it with one fasting overnight or meal-free late-afternoon observation before considering any basal edit.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The data show both overnight/early-morning lows and a recurring late-morning to afternoon rise, but the pattern is still confounded by corrections, temp targets, SMB/UAM, dynamic sensitivity, and absent meal logs. Because hypoglycemia risk is already meaningful, changing basal without a fasting-only check is not supported.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe one overnight fasting window and one meal-free late-afternoon interval with minimal corrections, then reassess basal only if the pattern repeats.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose is often near target, but lows also occur later in the night and early morning. The pattern is confounded by IOB, corrections, and temp targets, so a basal change at midnight is not supported yet.

Early-morning values do not show a clean isolated basal deficit or excess. Some low readings occur, but they overlap with automation and correction effects, so changing this segment would be speculative.
Morning glucose rises later in the day, but this segment cannot be separated from breakfast timing, corrections, and temp targets. The current evidence does not support a basal change here.

The late-morning rise could reflect basal, meal timing, or bolus timing. Because the dataset lacks meal logs and the period includes dynamic automation responses, the evidence is insufficient for a targeted basal change.

This is the most plausible basal candidate for the afternoon rise, but the same window also contains corrections, SMB/UAM, and variable IOB. A change is not yet supported without a fasting-like confirmation.
Evening lows appear in some days, but they are intertwined with post-correction and post-automation IOB. The evidence does not isolate this segment as the cause.
Time-below-range is elevated in the evening on some days, but the pattern is not cleanly basal-driven. Keeping this segment unchanged is safer until meal and correction timing are clearer.
No meal-linked data confirm whether this ratio is accurate. Correction variability and absent carb entries prevent isolating a true CR effect.
The early-morning CR cannot be tested from this dataset because there are no documented meal or carb entries. Any change would be unsupported and could worsen hypoglycemia risk.
Late-morning highs are present, but they are confounded by missing meal timing and correction activity. The current data do not separate meal bolus needs from basal or automation effects.
This is a plausible contributor to afternoon highs, but the same time block also includes temp targets, SMB/UAM, and delayed correction responses. Without meal logs, a change is not supported.
Evening meal effects cannot be separated from post-correction lows and IOB. The current evidence does not justify changing the evening ratio.
Correction responses vary widely and are heavily modified by dynamic sensitivity, SMB/UAM, and IOB. The evidence does not isolate an ISF problem strong enough to change it.
Because lows into the 40s are already present, lowering targets would increase risk. The current target is already conservative enough to avoid adding more hypoglycemia risk.

Morning and midday rises are present, but the evidence does not show that the target is the cause. Changing target would be a dependent adjustment best avoided until basal and meal timing are clearer.
Overnight lows make target reduction inappropriate, and raising the target would be a broader safety change not supported by the current evidence.

The long DIA is consistent with the observed delayed response variability and helps limit overcorrection risk. No evidence supports changing DIA before meal and correction timing are better characterized.
SMB and UAM are active and coherent with the observed loop behavior. Because lows are already present, changing this layer before basal and meal separation would increase risk without clear benefit.

The activation rules are internally consistent and match a non-meal-centric automation style. No material inconsistency or safety failure was found, and the main concern remains IOB accumulation during low-risk periods.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Observed rates and IOB stayed within the configured limits, so the current cadence is not obviously too aggressive. With existing hypoglycemia risk, changing these settings is not supported yet.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Observed enacted rates and IOB remain below the caps, so there is no evidence that ceiling limits are causing the pattern. The issue appears to be pattern attribution, not a hard limit.

Classic Autosens is intentionally off while dynamic sensitivity is active. The observed sensitivity_ratio of 1 is neutral, not disabled, and there is no evidence of a tuning error that justifies changing this group.
There are no carb treatment entries or e-carb records to validate a different absorption model. Changing these values without meal-linked evidence would be unsupported.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the current immediate bolus behavior at 100%, do not add routine prebolus or e-carbs from this dataset, and let SMB/UAM continue handling non-meal drift. Only consider a modest prebolus for predictable daytime meals if starting glucose is stable or rising and IOB is low; do not treat SMB/UAM as a substitute for meal timing.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: There is no declared meal strategy in analysis_context, no carb treatment entries, and no e-carb entries to validate a meal strategy change. The observed 4-6 hour variability is better explained by corrections, IOB, and automation than by a documented absorption problem. Because lows into the 40s mg/dL are present, broad prebolus or e-carb expansion would raise risk.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: A one-week log of meal timestamps, bolus timing relative to meals, and any rescue carb or e-carb use.

exceptions.pattern: Predictable daytime meals with repeated post-meal rise
exceptions.suggestion: Consider a small prebolus review only if glucose is stable or rising and active IOB is low.
exceptions.rationale: This is the only recurring pattern that might justify meal-timing adjustment, but the current dataset does not prove it.

exceptions.pattern: Meals occurring near lows or with active IOB
exceptions.suggestion: Avoid adding extra prebolus or e-carbs unless a recurrence is documented.
exceptions.rationale: The package already shows meaningful hypoglycemia risk, so this is the safer default.

implementation_steps: 1. Keep the current basal, CR, ISF, DIA, target, and AAPS automation settings unchanged.
2. Verify one fasting overnight or meal-free late-afternoon window before considering any basal change.
3. If a repeated pattern remains after the fasting check, review only one dependent parameter at a time.
4. Keep SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity unchanged while observing whether IOB accumulation coincides with lows.
5. Collect a one-week meal log with meal time, bolus time, and any rescue carb or e-carb use before discussing meal strategy changes.
education: A recurring rise in glucose does not automatically mean basal is too low; it can also come from meal timing, delayed absorption, or correction stacking.
SMB/UAM and dynamic sensitivity can help with drift, but they can also add IOB during vulnerable periods, so low-risk windows matter.
A long DIA can reduce overcorrection risk by keeping insulin on board longer in the model, which is useful when responses are variable.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; the user must verify every proposed change independently, one change at a time, with close glucose monitoring.
Do not change dependent settings together, because that makes it impossible to tell which change caused any glucose effect.
Because hypoglycemia is already present, any future change should be conservative and reviewed with the care team if needed.
